bottom_line: In COMET, carvedilol compared with metoprolol reduced all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 0.83 [95% CI 0.74–0.93]).
implications: These data support that, in this population and dosing strategy, carvedilol was associated with lower all-cause mortality than metoprolol (hazard ratio 0.83 [95% CI 0.74–0.93]), while the composite of all-cause mortality or all-cause admission was not significantly different (0.94 [0.86–1.02]). The reported safety event percentages (eg, serious bradycardia 3% in both groups) do not show a large between-group difference for these listed harms.

major_points.text: Multicentre, double-blind, randomised parallel-group trial comparing carvedilol vs metoprolol in chronic heart failure.
major_points.quote: In a multicentre, double-blind, and randomised parallel group trial, we assigned 1511 patients with chronic heart failure to treatment with carvedilol (target dose 25 mg twice daily) and 1518 to metoprolol (metoprolol tartrate, target dose 50 mg twice daily).

major_points.text: Participants had symptomatic chronic heart failure (NYHA II–IV), prior cardiovascular admission, and LVEF <0.35 on diuretics and ACE inhibitors unless not tolerated.
major_points.quote: Patients were required to have chronic heart failure (NYHA II–IV), previous admission for a cardio-vascular reason, an ejection fraction of less than 0·35, and to have been treated optimally with diuretics and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors unless not tolerated.

major_points.text: Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and the composite of all-cause mortality or all-cause admission; analysis was intention-to-treat.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or all-cause admission. Analysis was done by intention to treat.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with carvedilol than metoprolol with hazard ratio 0.83 (95% CI 0.74–0.93).
major_points.quote: The all-cause mortality was 34% (512 of 1511) for carvedilol and 40% (600 of 1518) for metoprolol (hazard ratio 0·83 [95% CI 0·74–0·93], p=0·0017).

major_points.text: The composite endpoint (mortality or all-cause admission) did not differ significantly between groups.
major_points.quote: The composite endpoint of mortality or all-cause admission occurred in 1116 (74%) of 1511 on carvedilol and in 1160 (76%) of 1518 on metoprolol (0·94 [0·86–1·02], p=0·122).

absolute_effects.text: All-cause mortality: 512 (34%) of 1511 vs 600 (40%) of 1518 (carvedilol vs metoprolol).
absolute_effects.quote: The all-cause mortality was 34% (512 of 1511) for carvedilol and 40% (600 of 1518) for metoprolol

absolute_effects.text: All deaths and all-cause admission: 1116 (74%) vs 1160 (76%) (carvedilol vs metoprolol).
Absolute reduction in mortality over 5 years was 5.7%.
absolute_effects.quote: The absolute reduction in mortality over 5 years was 5·7%.
